# Optional restrained treatment

Use only when the brief asks for a quiet, editorial or utilitarian interface.
Warm neutral surfaces, dark readable text, thin separators, flat components and
small semantic pastel accents are useful starting points. Existing brand colors,
fonts, icons and component conventions override this palette.

Create hierarchy through spacing and typography, not extra container layers.
Use restrained radii, minimal shadows and clear labels. Monospace or tabular
figures can help aligned data; editorial serif headings are an option when they
fit the brand. A bento grid is optional, not a default for every information task.

Keep links, focus and pressed states clear. Provide meaningful loading, empty and
error states. Prefer no motion when it adds no information; reduced-motion users
must retain all content and controls. Decorative backgrounds are unnecessary when
the request explicitly asks for flat or typography-only work.
